decisions.reason: As the former flagship and a strong fit with the firm's move toward cloud-based enterprise messaging, reduced standalone visibility more likely signals integration into the core offer than a result below aspiration.

After several years with no visible prominence, this adjacent document workflow service appears less central to the firm's strategic focus, so if its results stayed below aspiration management would redeploy resources to stronger messaging and new development projects.

The service still supports legacy email-fax interoperability valued by German business and public-sector customers, and its reuse of established capabilities gives enough slack to keep it unless performance clearly worsens.
As a close-to-core optimization feature for the existing fax business, it likely consumes limited additional resources and would usually be retained unless demand falls materially below aspiration.

Threat protection directly reinforces the firm's secure and compliant communications proposition, so management is likely to keep it and treat lower separate visibility as embedding into the broader platform rather than failure.
